text: Cao Bằng to host international seminar on cross-border economy, trade

CAO BẰNG - The northern province of Cao Bằng will host an international scientific seminar on cross-border economic and trade development on November 9, aiming to seek breakthrough solutions for border-gate economic development, logistics and tourism in the 2026-30 period.
The Cao Bằng People's Committee will organise the event, in coordination with Thuongmai University and Đại Đoàn Kết ( Great Solidarity ) newspaper.

It will bring together around 500 domestic and foreign delegates, including representatives of the government of China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, diplomatic agencies, associations and businesses operating in border-gate economic development and logistics.

The seminar is expected to connect policymakers, businesses and innovation initiatives, expand cooperation in trade and services, and promote the development of a modern, smart Cao Bằng Border Gate Economic Zone.
The programme will feature a plenary opening session, three parallel thematic sessions and a direct policy dialogue.

The first session, titled "Developing Border Gate Economic Zones amid Digital Transformation and Innovation", will examine development opportunities for Cao Bằng in connection with the Đồng Đăng-Trà Lĩnh expressway and propose models for smart border gates.
The second, "Developing Logistics Systems and Cross-Border E-commerce", will focus on investment needs for logistics infrastructure and mechanisms to promote cross-border e-commerce.

The third session, "Expanding Cross-Border Cooperation in Trade, Services and Tourism" will seek solutions for sustainable border tourism and more effective promotion of the Bản Giốc-Detian Waterfall Scenic Area and the Non Nước Cao Bằng UNESCO Global Geopark.
A highlight will be a policy dialogue and business networking session between Vietnamese and Chinese enterprises, chaired by the Chairman of the Cao Bằng People's Committee.

The provincial authorities will introduce a list of priority projects seeking investment and witness the signing of memoranda of understanding (MoUs) between businesses from the two countries in import-export activities, border-gate infrastructure and logistics.

On the sidelines, the organisers will arrange an exhibition showcasing the province's key products, business-to-business (B2B) networking activities and field trips to major border gates and the Pắc Bó historical site. - VNA/VNS
